grade.first_issue: In Case 2, the assertion that the distance from x0 to the forward progression {y+n c(y): n∈N} is at most c(y) is unjustified and generally false when y>x0.
grade.summary: The claimed classification is correct, and the proof correctly establishes defect invariance, nonnegativity, equality of all positive defect values, and the converse. However, the sole argument excluding coexistence of zero and positive defects relies on a false distance claim. Consequently, neither c(y)≥4x0 nor the subsequent propagation of the zero set follows. This is a decisive compatibility gap under Rule E, so the score is capped at 3. A repair would require a separate argument, such as proving the zero- and positive-defect level sets are both relatively open and invoking connectedness.
strengths: Correctly derives f(f(x))=2f(x)-x, c(f(x))=c(x), the iterate formula, and c(x)≥0.
Correctly obtains the estimate |c(x)-c(z)|≤(sqrt(x)-sqrt(z))^2 on the image and uses orbit approximation to show all positive defect values agree.
Correctly verifies that every f(x)=x+c with c≥0 satisfies both inequalities.

errors.description: For a forward arithmetic progression y+nC, if y>x0 then its distance from x0 is at least y-x0, which need not be at most C. No preceding argument establishes y≤x0. This false assertion is load-bearing: without it, the mixed case c∈{0,C} is not eliminated, so the final constancy conclusion is unsupported.
